For this assignment, we will use tidyverse, quanteda, quanteda.textstats, and quanteda.textmodels. You will also need quanteda.textmodels to load one of the datasets.

## Frequency analysis

For this bit, we will work with the Irish budget debate speeches dataset. You can find that dataset in the quanteda.textmodels package. It is called "data_corpus_irishbudget2010" (see the Session 5 example script for more info) and you can load it the same way that we usually load the presidential speeches. 

1) Load the dataset, tokenize it, and create a DFM with stopwords removed. Then, create a dataframe with the 5 most common words for each party and print it.

2) Create a word cloud showing the 10 most commonly used words from each party. How useful do you find this plot?

## Keyness analysis

3) Load the US Presidential speeches dataset and tokenize it. Remove stopwords and punctuation. Run a chi-squared keyness analysis to determine the most Democrat and Republican words respectively, and plot the results. Remember that there used to be parties that were neither Democrat nor Republican (you don't have to present keyness results for them)!

4) How many words are there that are associated with the Republican party at a 95% significance level (i.e. p <= .05)?

## Complexity

5) Plot the type-token-ratio of the 10 Presidential speeches with the highest TTRs, using a dot plot with the speech on the y axis and the TTR on the x axis.

6) Calculate the readability of every speech twice, once using the Flesch-Kincaid method and once using the Dale-Chall method. Create a scatterplot with the results of one method on the x axis and the results of the other on the y-axis, and add a trend line. What do you notice?
